images.text: A new manual needs to be designed to explain the CBIS. The abbreviation CBIS stands for Computer Based Information System although not many people call it that way. Due to the nature of our business, it is important to understand what CBIS means to our company. A CBIS uses computer technology to carry out certain pieces of work. However, computers are not understood as the only source of hardware used in an information system. Thus, a single computer is not included; in fact, it can even incorporate hundreds of computers, printers, and databases, among other devices to create a system.

In case you wonder about the basic components of information systems, here's some information. We'll start with resources of people where end-users and IS specialists, system analysts, programmers, and data administrators are included. Computer equipment and associate devices, machines and media, which are recognized as hardware, are the next important parts to point at within the components of CBISs. We also need to take into account software, that is, programs and procedures. Last, but not least, we have data and networks. Within data, we are considering data itself and knowledge bases, whereas communications media and network support cannot be left aside from networks.

<div align="justify">Each one of these components offers particular characteristics. For example, end users, that is to say, accountants, salespeople, engineers, clerks, customers, or managers, are known as clients. The IS Specialists, on the other hand, are people who develop and operate information systems. Evidently, clients are not included in this group; only systems analysts, programmers, computer operators, and other related IS personnel are taken into account. When it comes to hardware resources, computers and other equipment are used. As for software, physical devices are not taken into consideration, it only considers programs and operating systems. Now, all of this is not written yet, we just have a sketch. I need the design team to put everything in a printed version.

Simple Present Passive in Negative Statements

We use the passive voice when the emphasis within a sentence is on the object rather than on the subject. With this in mind, the verb construction necessarily changes to always having the verb to be preceding the past participle form of the main verb.
A single computer is not included, it can include even hundreds of computers.
However, computers are not understood as the only source of hardware used in an information system.
Communications media and network support are not excluded as a data and network component.

Take a look at the following passive voice sentences in the present simple.

D.O. = Direct Object

AFFIRMATIVE

Structure:
D.O. + am / is / are + verb (participle form) + complement.

Example:
Programs are created to make customers' lives easier.

NEGATIVE

Structure:
D.O. + am not / isn't / aren't + verb (participle form) + complement.

Example:
Data centers aren't designed for big companies only.
A computer-based information system (CBIS) uses computer technology to perform some specific tasks.
A computer based information system has some basic components. Take a look at the following chart; it gives you detailed information about such components.
